command_lint.cc: after conversion, no std::cerr, only std::cout. Update include comment to `// std::cout`. Actually the include is still needed for std::cout. Change comment.

command_bundle.cc: add `#include "logger.h"` in local includes; iostream comment already `// std::cout`.

command_validate.cc: unchanged include comment.

resolver.h: after conversion no std::cerr named; but does resolver.h use std::cout? No. Does it need iostream at all? It may need std::ostream? No usage. But removing the include is risky (transitive). Better to keep include but update comment. Hmm, if no iostream entity used, clang-format won't care about comment. But is there another use? Let me check resolver.h fully for ostream/endl. grep showed none besides. However, resolver.h might use std::ostringstream? Let me grep. Not shown. So iostream maybe unneeded but keeping is safe. Upstream probably changed comment to remove std::cerr or removed include. I'll keep it but not worry much. Actually the style guideline says new includes go with include block — not about removing.

I think safest minimal: leave include lines mostly, only add logger.h where needed and update stale comments where obviously wrong. Actually changing comment is cosmetic but consistent. Hmm "no drive-by reformatting" — comments aren't reformatting. I'll update command_lint.cc comment to `// std::cout` since std::cerr is gone. For resolver.h, `// std::cerr` is now wrong; but maybe still needed for nothing. I'd keep `<iostream>` (to avoid breaking transitive compile) and update comment to something? If nothing from iostream is used, comment could be removed entirely: `#include <iostream>` but clang-format might reorder? It won't. Actually leaving a stale comment is worse. But safest is to not touch to minimize diff. Hmm.

Let me check resolver.h more thoroughly for iostream usage.
